text.p: These are the main stories in Slovenia's newspapers this Monday:
- Parliament is expected to vote on Monday on whether to change the constitution to enable foreigners to buy land in Slovenia.
- Slovenian rower Iztok Cop won a singles world cup competition in Luzern on Sunday.
- The government said it would announce a public tender for the construction of a new court in Ljubljana.

- Inspectors have started legal proceedings against 152 restaurants for breaching the new tobacco law, which obliges all restaurants to be divided into smoking and non-smoking areas. The law was adopted in November.

- The agriculture ministry said Slovenia would only be able to liberalise agricultural trade with the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) countries from the year 2001. CEFTA comprises Slovenia, the Czech Republic, Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and Romania.
- U.S. State Secretary Madeleine Albright said Slovenia was the strongest candidate for the next round of NATO expansion. Albright paid a one-day visit to Slovenia on Saturday.
- General Albin Gutman, head of the Slovenian armed forces, visited the Slovenian unit participating in an international peace-keeping mission in Albania.
- Hail on Sunday caused severe damage to farms in Prekmurje, Eastern Slovenia.
- Slovenian Railways has introduced discounts of up to 50 percent for young travellers during summer.
